documentary_notes: Qilu is producer; Química Haller is registrant/packager/distributor and cover identity. Preserve manifest manufacturer. Exclusively IV/professional handling, not self-injection.

Cover says above 12 years, while body contains younger pediatric indications/doses. No question reconciles these scopes. Adult renal-table context was visually checked; no personal dose is calculated.

Traditional herbal patient leaflet, two-column layout. Native glyph encoding contains visible-text substitutions (for example proėssional and inespecíėca). References retain literal extracted glyphs and explicit source-column regions; visual source was checked on both pages. No PDF or production parser was edited.

Wesp appears in legal text; no explicit producer role is invented and empty manifest manufacturer remains empty. Adult above-16 label coexists with under-16 contraindication; no question targets exactly age 16. Claimed unreported product reactions coexist with known constituent reactions; no question generalizes safety.

After-opening shelf life is not inferred from expiry since manufacture. General herbal/co-medication warnings do not identify a probiotic. Negative absence requires independent human full-document confirmation.
Halex Istar is source identity; explicit manufacturer field remains empty. Product is hospital-restricted, rectal and individualized, despite water-for-injection excipient wording.

Section 2 says no sensitive colic/irritation whereas section 8 lists colic/diarrhea. Q08 retains a human audit flag; no clinical reconciliation. Empty overdose line and incomplete telephone text are not repaired externally.
Disposal of residual solution does not specify collection destination for used materials. No procedural fasting protocol is supplied.

documentary_notes: One PDF contains Atrovent nebulization drops on physical pages 1-5 and Atrovent N aerosol on pages 6-11, followed by shared history. Preserve local presentation, age, route and different device instructions.

Drops and aerosol have different producers; frozen multi-manufacturer field unchanged. Mask instructions are for drops, cleaning is for aerosol mouthpiece; neither establishes spacer-mask or nebulizer-cup disinfection instructions.

Immediate ophthalmologist contact and rapid respiratory-worsening instructions are safety audit priorities. Instructions for empty-canister estimation are not turned into general device calibration rules.
Colpatrin is vaginal cream for adults; treatment application is not oral ingestion. Teuto is explicitly registrant/producer.

Preserve timing of menstruation relative to already-started treatment, minimum post-treatment alcohol interval, disposable applicators and risk to latex barriers. Latex precaution is supported positive evidence, not a missing-material negative.

The source includes systemic-metronidazole and oral-overdose discussions within a vaginal-product leaflet. No question silently translates them into systemic dosing or partner treatment. Source immune/skin and mental-health warning text remains documentary content, not individualized clinical advice.

EMS appears in cover/legal identification; explicit producer role is not inferred and empty manifest manufacturer stays empty. Five grams is sachet powder mass, 500 mg is paracetamol; query presentation distinguishes sachets without leaking requested administration facts.

Section 3 contraindicates under 12 but section 6 mentions a medical exception; no question resolves that conflict. Renal/hepatic caution and prohibition language also coexist. Adverse frequency labels contain inconsistent rare/common descriptions; no frequency question is authored.
Overdose requires immediate care even without symptoms. Laboratory assay interference is not a general antidoping conclusion.

Teuto 50 mg/mL oral suspension is not the other corpus's ibuprofen presentation. Physical page 5 repeats low/high fever table columns in two panels; Q05 uses 20 kg row and ≥39°C column without deriving a new dose.

Different general duration statements (pain ten days, fever three days, seven-day overall caution) are not reconciled. Under-six-month contraindication remains distinct from under-two-year medical supervision.

Immediate suspension/medical assistance for allergy is retained. General cautions about combined analgesics and dehydration do not supply an alternating-dose or vomiting-redose protocol; negative boundaries are flagged.
Eurofarma is explicitly registrant/producer. Sodium naproxen amount 550 mg corresponds to 500 mg naproxen; do not conflate forms.

Section 6 gives ten-day language but next physical page has seven-day warning; no duration question selects a clinically preferred value. Adult label and younger-child exception also coexist. Some tabulated adverse-event wording is malformed; no question repairs it.

Section 7 says seek professional guidance only, not a take/skip protocol. Negative Q09 concerns that missing decision, not absence of all advice. Lactation contraindication includes explicit alternative-treatment/feed support.

Low-dose aspirin interaction specifies uncertain clinical relevance; do not equate laboratory pharmacodynamic interaction with a quantified clinical outcome. Food allowance does not override stomach restrictions.
Halex Istar is source identity, not an inferred manufacturer role. Ampoules are specifically IM/adult and single-use.
Injectable-specific under-18 restriction differs from generic diclofenac under-14/juvenile-arthritis wording. Hepatic/renal monitoring coexists with contraindications; Q05 preserves that caution.

Text discussing injectable treatment beyond four weeks coexists with section-6 maximum two days. No duration question silently resolves this major source tension. Do not provide self-injection or home management of local complications.
Section 8 serious skin/mucosal reactions require immediate professional contact. Contraception and hot-versus-cold compress management are not documented.
Vitamedic is explicitly registrant/producer. Pack sizes 492/504 appear in this source and are not silently corrected to conventional pack sizes.
Different onset for pain and fever, adolescent viral-symptom restriction, hepatic no-rechallenge condition and losartan interaction retain their local scopes.

Milk excretion is described as unestablished and later as established; no lactation question resolves that tension. Dose text permits half tablets and exceptional higher dosing; no new personal regimen is generated.
Viral-illness restriction is not vaccination postponement. Oral tablet instructions do not establish feeding-tube preparation.
